prerequisites: First and second principle of thermodynamics

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanical systems and machines.

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering for the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to interpret technical projects and reports.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to solve problems effectively.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Information search and management skills.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop interpersonal skills.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the ability for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Ability to generate new ideas (creativity).
Understand the fundamental principles of fluid mechanics applied to the operation of hydraulic machines.
Identify and classify different hydraulic machines, distinguishing between generating and receiving machines, as well as between positive displacement machines and turbomachines.
Analyze the energetic and fluid dynamic behavior of pumps, turbines, and other hydraulic equipment through the application of fundamental equations of conservation of mass, energy, and momentum.
Interpret characteristic curves and operating parameters of hydraulic pumps and turbines, evaluating their performance and optimal operating conditions.
Select appropriate hydraulic machines based on the technical needs of an industrial, energy, or supply installation.
Evaluate head losses and phenomena associated with fluid transport in conduits and hydraulic systems.
Apply similarity criteria and dimensional analysis in the study and design of hydraulic machines.
Understand cavitation, regulation, and stability phenomena, as well as their effects on machine performance and lifespan.
Perform basic design and sizing calculations for hydraulic installations and associated equipment.
Use computer tools and experimental techniques for the analysis and resolution of problems related to hydraulic machines.
Develop technical work capacity and critical analysis, interpreting experimental results and proposing efficient and sustainable solutions.
Appreciate energy efficiency and environmental impact associated with the use of hydraulic machines in industrial and energy applications.

syllabus_topics: General concepts of fluid mechanics for fluid machines
General equation of turbomachines. Similarity equations
Calculation and sizing of pumping systems
Calculation and sizing of ventilation systems
Introduction to the study of electricity demand
Hydroelectric energy in the electricity generation mix
Equation of the conservation of angular momentum
Comparison of volumetric and centrifugal pumps
Influence of the inlet blade angle
Influence of the outlet blade angle
Calculation of the actual curve in radial pumps
teaching_methods: Practical classes (problem-solving, modeling and simulation with EES software)
Integrative project (team-based analysis, modeling, and simulation of a fluid-mechanical system)
Autonomous student work (study, problem-solving, project development, report writing, exam preparation)

assessment_methods.method: Problem-solving and practical case tests (using EES software)

assessment_rules: The continuous assessment system is composed of problem-solving tests (30%), theoretical knowledge tests (30%), continuous assessment questionnaires (10%), and an integrative project (30%). Problem-solving tests and theoretical knowledge tests require a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 to be considered passed. If an overall grade of 5.0 or higher is achieved but any minimum is not met, the final grade will be 4.9. In the second call, only unpassed tests/activities need to be redone; grades for continuous assessment questionnaires and the integrative project are retained from the first call and are not recoverable.
